abstract.text: A model is a base class for stateful operations on a dynamic graph. It can be
use to construct computations statically, thus, more efficient.
Multiply all values with a constant.
Hyper-connection split, fused pre-weighted residual reduction, or expansion.
Forward-only, parameter-free Sol approximate attention with exactly three inputs: Q, K, V.
Whether to enable gradient checkpointing for this model. Once it is enabled, we will re-run
the model forward pass again during backward pass. This is effective at reducing memory usage.
The minimum occurrence index for this model’s name when generating parameter names.
Defaults to zero and must be nonnegative. Models with the same name in the same naming
scope continue counting above previously assigned indices. This setting does not propagate
to children and must be set before compiling the enclosing model. The getter returns the
configured minimum, not the index assigned during compilation.

A model that applies another model independently across replicated inputs.
Whether the existing model is for testing or training.
Emulates a lower-precision data format while retaining the input storage datatype.
Abstract representation of the stateful components from the model.
Gate and up projections followed by optionally clamped SwiGLU.
Stages all three MoE projection tables together. Decode keeps one resident
pool and rewrites routing outputs to its physical slots. Prefill compacts
the active experts into durable gate, up, and down staging buffers.
The masked fill model. If the value equal to a given constant, fill with another constant.
Broadly speaking, you can have two types of parameters, weight and bias.
You can get them in abstract fashion with this method.
Div two inputs together. It will not do broadcast.
Raise every element in an input to the specified exponent.
Complex number multiplication over two inputs, optionally conjugating the right input.
Specify the maximum number of streams we need to allocate to run this model.
Walsh-Hadamard transform over the last dimension.

RMSNorm followed by a swish-gated multiply.
RMSNorm followed by a complex multiply.
A segmented linear layer model that makes more sense in the lenses of MoE.
The size of scratch memory allocated for this model.
Whether to enable memory reduction for this model. The current supported memory reduction
technique is to redo datatype conversion during backward pass if needed.
Make a copy of the model. This won’t copy over the parameters. If you want, you need to copy
The flags for the underlying execution node.
Square root of a input. It will not do broadcast.
Whether this is initialized as trainable model or not.
Selects and groups routed MoE experts. With
remains one row for a broadcast-capable expert operation; larger inputs are
probability sum plus epsilon. Zero retains the denominator floor of 2^-14.
A model is a base class for stateful operations on a dynamic graph. It can be
use to construct computations statically, thus, more efficient.
Add two inputs together. It will do broadcast if needed.
You can compose a new model from old models when applying IO on them.
Two segmented expert projections followed by weighted, clamped SwiGLU.
Make the input tensor to be 1-D tensor (respecting N).
Multiply two inputs together. It will do broadcast if needed.
A IO class represent the abstract input / output for a model. It can correspond
to one or more tensors when the model is materialized.
You can compose a new model of a list of models assuming one’s output is another’s input.
IDs are sorted ascending, followed by -1 padding.
